posts.heading: September 14, 2026
posts.text:
By 07:26, the first Blue Jay had landed, marking the station’s first confident visual record of a Northern Bobwhite shortly after. The morning built quickly on the strength of the Tufted Titmouse, which has since visited 64 times, often in direct competition with Carolina Chickadees who have logged 46 confident visits.

This is the busiest morning so far, with 159 feeder visits far exceeding the recent daily average of 39. The Carolina Wren, though seen only six times, has been the dominant voice in the air, accounting for 160 detections since sunrise.

The steady stream of Tufted Titmice and Carolina Chickadees has kept the tube feeder busy, while Mourning Doves have made 14 confident visits to the ground-level stations.
